newsitem.title: USA: Sun International sets $500 mln hotel plan.
newsitem.headline: Sun International sets $500 mln hotel plan.

text.p: Sun International Hotels Limited said on Monday it had a $500 million development plan for the Resorts Casino Hotel in Atlantic City, acquired via its merger with Griffin Gaming & Entertainment Inc.

Sun International said it completed the previously announced merger with Griffin, which owns Resorts Casino Hotel. The Bahamas-based company said the deal positioned it as a major casino operator on the eastern U.S. coast.

Chairman Sol Kerzner said as part of the development plan for Resorts Casino, the hotel would be transformed into a mega-resort with an ocean theme based on the Lost City of Atlantis. One of its features will be the world's largest indoor living tidal coral reef, he said.

"We expect to apply this knowledge to developing a resort in which the marine features and aquariums will be the largest on the East Coast of the U.S., or almost twice the size of the National Aquarium in Baltimore," Kerzner said.
He was referring to research done for the company's Atlantis Resort on Paradise Island, Bahamas.

The existing Resorts Casino hotel would be renovated and a new development would be built on adjacent real estate, Sun said. About 1,400 new hotel rooms would be constructed, it said. The project was due to open around Christmas 1999.
